Four major corium forms identified: (1) Elephant's Foot - extremely hard black lava 180t at lowest level; (2) brown lava flows on walls/floors; (3) stalactites; (4) ceramic fuel particles in dust. Elephant's Foot = ~180t dense glass-like material

Room 305/2 and corium locations: k_eff < 1.0 (subcritical) but neutron counts doubled 2016-2021 as NSC excluded water (FCM drying → less neutron moderation → BUT better geometry may increase criticality approach). Ukrainian physicists monitoring. k_eff estimates 0.4-0.8 in various models.

NSC installation 2016 excluded rainfall → corium FCM dried out → reduced neutron moderation → changed criticality parameters. This is the mechanism behind Room 305/2 neutron increase 2016-2021. Water acts as neutron moderator; removing it shifts spectrum harder BUT also reduces moderation so neutron multiplication can change.

Elephant's Foot measured >10,000 R/hr (=100 Sv/hr) when first accessed Dec 1986; lethal dose in seconds; robot camera sent first; dose reduced to ~800 R/hr by 1990 as short-lived fission products decayed

Current accessible areas near corium (~500 R/hr in 1986 → ~34 µSv/hr in 2026); 140,000-fold reduction in 40 years due to fission product decay; still inaccessible direct contact; remote tools required

Chernobylite: new mineral phase identified in Chernobyl corium; complex silicate containing U Zr Si O; formed at ~2000°C when molten fuel contacted concrete; named after the accident; first artificial mineral recognized in nature

Corium lava = heterogeneous mixture: UO2 (fuel) + ZrO2 + Fe oxides + Cr oxides + Si oxides (from structural materials/concrete) + fission products incorporated in glass matrix; hot particulates = pure fuel particles; not a single phase material
